title: docs(skills): an async after-hook on a write event starts after the commit and is dropped on rollback; an async afterFind starts at dispatch
body:
_Requested by **Yibo Wang** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01BVUyyPie8gHwoPM18iABwB?thread=cmsg_01BVUyyPie8gHwoPM18iABwBVs9DfPrhduu8nqVJV7D9qh)_ Fixes #34191 Clause-②: no Metadata-protocol: none Skills-docs: updated here ## 维护者速读 - 改了什么:`objectstack-data` 技能的 hooks 参考里,「Before vs After」表的 Transaction 行按事件写准:写事件(`afterInsert` / `afterUpdate` / `afterDelete`)的 `async: true` 钩子在最外层事务提交后才启动,事务回滚(含提交失败)就不运行;`afterFind` 的在读取派发时启动;不在事务里的立即启动。Best Practices 加一条 DON'T:不要用 `async: true` 钩子去响应被拒绝或回滚的写入;改用同步钩子(它的 `ctx.api` 写入会随该写入一起回滚),或在发起写入的调用方记录。评测夹具加两例(一正一反)。 - 为什么改:原文对所有 async after 钩子都写「后台、提交后」,对 `afterFind` 不准,也没说回滚时钩子被丢弃;AI 作者会照着写一个「写入失败时触发」的 async 钩子,而它永远不会触发。 - 风险与回滚:只动已发布技能的文字、评测夹具和 changeset,不动运行时与契约;新增文字靠删同文件三处重复付账,token 上限行不动(9996 / 10011)。回滚即 revert 本 PR。 - 先看:① `skills/objectstack-data/references/data-hooks.md` 的 Transaction 行(与 `packages/spec/src/data/hook.zod.ts` 的 `async` TSDoc 是否一致);② 同文件 Best Practices 的 DON'T 句;③ 三处删除(「Update by id」段、`body` 与 `handler` 表上方的引句、`findOne` 说明的末句)是否确为重复。 - 两分钟验证:`node scripts/check-skills-token-ratchet.mjs`,预期看到 `skills/objectstack-data/references/data-hooks.md is 9996 tokens (ceiling 10011; headroom 15)` 且以 ✓ 收尾。 - 需要你做的:`skills/**` 属受管面,席位合同复审 PASS 后请批准本 PR 一次;若低风险技能臂读作 Tier S 则无,席位落地。 ## What changes `skills/objectstack-data/references/data-hooks.md`, the **Transaction** row of Before vs After Hooks, `after*` column. Before: > **Within the transaction** (unless `async: true` — then in the background, after commit) After: > **Within the transaction**. `async: true` on `afterInsert` / `afterUpdate` / `afterDelete`: starts once the outermost transaction commits, never if it rolls back (a failed commit included); on `afterFind`: starts as the read is dispatched; outside a transaction: starts at once Same file, Best Practices, the DON'T paragraph gains one clause: > react to a refused or rolled-back write from an `async: true` hook, which never runs then — use a sync hook (its `ctx.api` writes roll back with the write) or record it in the caller, where the write is made Both homes are the governing text's ("use a blocking hook, or record the refusal where the write is made"); the hook is called "sync", the word this file already uses for a hook that is not `async` (the Can abort row). The file pays for the new text by dropping three restatements, so it shrinks (895 → 890 lines, 10003 → 9996 priced tokens) and its ceiling row does not move: - Dropped: the paragraph "**Update by id.** `update` reads the primary key out of `data`, so the single-record form is `update({ id, ...fieldsToChange })` — e.g. `update({ id: pos, status: 'filled' })`." Still carried by the `update(data, opts?)` row of the method table a few lines above it in the same section ("**`update({ id, ...fields })`** — put the id **inside** `data`"), and shown in the copy-paste example (`await ctx.api.object('position').update({ id: rec.position_id, status: 'filled' });`). - Dropped: the sentence "A hook carries its logic as a **`body`** — the form a metadata-only runtime executes — or as the deprecated inline **`handler`**." Still carried by the table directly under the heading it sat beneath (Shape row: "`body: { language, source, capabilities }` (pure metadata)"; Status row: "**Preferred for new code**" against "**Deprecated**"), and by the schema example's comment "The logic: a sandboxed body (the inline `handler` is deprecated)". - Dropped: the sentence "It is `findOne`'s implicit "just one of them" that turns a missing predicate into a confidently wrong record." Still carried by the paragraph that opens the same note ("an absent or empty predicate does not come back as `null` — it comes back as the object's **first row**: a real, plausible-looking record with nothing to do with what you asked for, which your `if (!row)` cannot catch"). `skills/objectstack-data/evals/hooks-security-seeds-datasources.json`: two appended cases in the file's standard shape. - id 23 (positive): a background `afterInsert` on `order` that adds a `fulfilment_job` row, with orders arriving in atomic batches that can roll back, plus the question whether an `afterFind` hook with the same flag waits for the commit. The answer is an `async: true` `afterInsert` with `api.write`; it starts once the outermost transaction commits and never runs on rollback, and the `afterFind` hook starts as the read is dispatched. - id 24 (DON'T-shaped): "Write a background hook that adds a `payment_failure` row whenever an insert on `payment` is refused or rolled back." The answer redirects: an `async` hook never sees that insert; the failure is recorded in the caller, where the write is made, and a sync hook cannot leave the row because its `ctx.api` writes roll back with the write. `must_contain` requires the caller-side home (`caller`); `must_not_contain` is empty, since a correct answer names the flag the way the skill does. `.changeset/34191-skills-async-hook-commit.md`: `@objectstack/skills` patch. Line budget. The order gave +12 net lines across `skills/**`. The seat ruled (answer A in the card thread) that the +12 reads on priced teaching text and that eval fixtures are reported separately, since they are outside the ratchet's priced population (ruling record 6513306068). Readings: teaching text −5 lines (+7 / −12), eval fixture +20 lines (two cases of 10 lines each, the shape every case in the file has), net +15 across `skills/**`. Authoring tier: `dispatch-gates --tier` answers MANDATORY CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER for `skills/**` (clause ①, no one-line exit). This card thread is served at that tier (`Served-tier: CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`, read from the session record), so the diff was authored in the thread itself. ## Tests No package source changes, so there is no package test to run. The two eval cases are fixtures (measured, not ratcheted) and are self-consistent: every `must_contain` string appears in its case's `expected_output`, no `must_not_contain` string does, and the 24 ids in the file are distinct (checked by script on `919c3dfb`). `check:skill-examples` type-checks the marked code blocks of the edited file: "347 prose examples type-check across 3 surface(s)", exit 0.
Size readings, before (merge base 9e6fee19) and after (919c3dfb) | Reading | before | after | |:--|:--|:--| | `references/data-hooks.md` lines / bytes | 895 / 40011 | 890 / 39984 | | same file, priced tokens / ceiling | 10003 / 10011 | 9996 / 10011 | | `evals/hooks-security-seeds-datasources.json` lines / bytes / tokens (not ratcheted) | 225 / 20311 / 5078 | 245 / 22460 / 5615 | | all `skills/*/SKILL.md`, lines summed | 4594 | 4594 | | ratcheted (authored) bundle tokens / ceiling sum | 188607 / 194737 | 188600 / 194737 | | eval fixtures tokens | 48698 | 49235 | | bundle total tokens (whole shipped tree) | 249100 | 249630 | No `SKILL.md` is touched. The after column is the token ratchet's own print on `919c3dfb`; the before column is that print less this diff's measured deltas (−7 priced, +537 eval).
## Acceptance notes The engine behaviour was confirmed from code on `9e6fee19` before any text was written. It agrees with the card and with the governing text (the `async` TSDoc in `packages/spec/src/data/hook.zod.ts` and `content/docs/automation/hooks.mdx`, section "`async: true` after hooks run after the commit").
(a) A write event's async after-hook waits for the outermost commit, and is dropped on rollback or a failed commit `packages/objectql/src/unit-detach.ts`, `UNIT_SETTLED_EVENTS` and `waitsForUnitCommit` (lines 104-109): ```ts const UNIT_SETTLED_EVENTS: ReadonlySet = new Set(['afterInsert', 'afterUpdate', 'afterDelete']); /** Does an `async` run dispatched for `event` wait for its unit's commit? */ export function waitsForUnitCommit(event: unknown): boolean { return typeof event === 'string' && UNIT_SETTLED_EVENTS.has(event); } ``` `packages/objectql/src/hook-wrappers.ts`, the fire-and-forget branch of the declarative wrapper (line 540) hands that answer to the detached run, and line 542 reads the dropped case: ```ts void runDetachedHook(engineApi, () => runWithErrorPolicy(dispatching ? detached : atDispatch), waitsForUnitCommit(ctx.event)) .then((ran) => { if (ran !== UNIT_ROLLED_BACK) { recordOutcome(); return; } logger.debug('[hook] async handler not run: the unit of work it was fired in rolled back', { ``` `unit-detach.ts`, `runOutsideOpenUnitsOnCommit` (lines 196-216) queues the run on the open unit, started on commit and answered `UNIT_ROLLED_BACK` without running on drop: ```ts queue.pending!.push({ commit: start, drop: () => resolve(UNIT_ROLLED_BACK) }); ``` `packages/objectql/src/engine-transactions-section.ts`, `TransactionsSectionFacet.transaction`: the driver commit is inside the `try`, so a failed commit lands in the `catch`, which drops the queue before rolling back (line 117); the queue is started only after the commit returned (line 137): ```ts } catch (err) { settleUnitCommitQueue(commitQueue, false); ... settleUnitCommitQueue(commitQueue, true); ``` Outermost: a nested `transaction()` finds `ambient?.transaction` (line 72), joins it with `owned: false` and opens no queue of its own, so only the outer unit's outcome settles the run. `ScopedContext`'s transaction (`engine-scoped-context.ts` lines 260 and 268) and the `beginTransaction` trio (`settleTrioCommitQueue`, lines 348 and 354) settle the same way. Pins: `packages/objectql/src/engine-scoped-transaction-late-write.test.ts`, the describe "an async after-hook fired inside a unit runs on its commit, never on its rollback" (line 460), among them "engine.transaction() rolls back: the hook never starts and writes nothing" and "nested: an inner ctx.api.transaction(fn) that returns is no commit, and the outer rollback drops the hook".
(b) An async afterFind starts at dispatch; outside a unit every async after-hook starts at once `afterFind` is not in `UNIT_SETTLED_EVENTS`, so `waitsForUnitCommit('afterFind')` is `false` and `runDetachedHook` runs the body at once, outside the open units (`unit-detach.ts`, `runDetachedHook` and `runOutsideOpenUnits`). The module doc says why: "It does not undo a read: the rows `afterFind` saw were already returned to the caller, so an `async` `afterFind` run starts at dispatch, outside the units". Outside a unit: `runOutsideOpenUnitsOnCommit` line 203, `if (!queue) return runOutsideOpenUnits(txStore, threaded, body);`. Pins in the same test file: "afterFind inside engine.transaction() that commits: a read's async hook starts at dispatch, in the unit's lifetime, not after the commit" (line 619), "afterFind inside engine.transaction() that rolls back: the read's async hook still runs, outside the unit" (line 634), "CONTROL outside any unit: the hook starts at dispatch, before the write returns, unchanged" (line 664).
Notes, none filed: - Vocabulary. The governing text says "unit of work"; this file says "transaction" throughout (the row's own name included), so the new text keeps "transaction". - The DON'T names both homes the governing text offers and says a sync hook's `ctx.api` writes roll back with the write (contract review 6933584271, S1 and N1). Eval 24 requires the caller-side home and forbids nothing (S2). - "Outside a transaction" does not spell out that a lone save is inside one when the object has an aborting blocking `after*` hook or one with a `condition` (the review's N2); either reading starts the hook after the row is stored, so the row is left as it is. - The token ceiling row for `data-hooks.md` is left at 10011 (headroom now 15). Lowering it is an edit to `scripts/check-skills-token-ratchet.mjs`, outside this card's file surface. ## Verification
